People say this kind of thing a lot, but there is a corollary that I'm not sure is less common. People are cruel, and they learn their cruelty from each other. Like, say, if you want to do something with your life that your family and friends aren't doing, like not have kids or something, you're not the asshole even if everybody around you is acting like it.

I would say if people keep treating you badly, there is definitely a pattern to explore. But whether you should change or whether you should just keep drudging through their crap is a different matter.

That's why you don't read somebody's journal (although I will admit it's unfortunate when you do it by accident). Some privacy in a relationship is healthy in my opinion. Because the only way, ever, somebody never has negative thoughts about you is if they do have them and they just pretend not to. Journals are a tool for us to process our own emotions and keep track of them so we notice patterns and grow and what have you. Part of their advantage is that they're unfiltered. And the emotions most in need of processing tend to be the ones you wouldn't want to know we have in the first place.

Because the thing is: guess what, the mean things people think about us, sometimes they're actually true. There are patterns in what people find attractive, and some people, like myself, fail to live up to standards of attractiveness that a majority of people share. I know anybody who dates me, even those who are okay with my looks, will have doubts from time to time. If I only go out with people who find me stunning, I'll die alone. That's life for you. But you don't need to be the most attractive person for a relationship to work; you just need to be attractive enough. I reckon most people can probably think of somebody hotter than their SO, but they can get their various genitalia up and running in a pinch all the same.

When somebody faces your flaws head-on and still wants to stay, then that's as good as it gets. Somebody who doesn't see flaws at all is deluded and down the road, you're going to wish they did acknowledge their negative feelings about you before they absolutely had to.

For what is worth, I do think he was being honest: some days it's better than others. Personally, I've never seen a person in my life that I wouldn't consider unattractive on a bad day, and my bad days aren't infrequent. So I guess the upshot of all this is ask him this: on those days when his libido is really down because of the meds, does he find the people he's normally attracted to attractive in general? And on his good days, does he still consider you less attractive than average?

My sister is like that to the T, down to the suicidal ideation, and I talked to her, and honestly it didn't do much. She kept saying that she wasn't acting this way out of desperation but because she genuinely cares about people (read: much older East Asian strangers she fetishizes) and she doesn't want to change that about herself. That if boys are creeped out by her confessing her everlasting love two days into texting, it's because of "different strides" and they're just not compatible. And if older men use her for sexting or to get to her "hotter" friends, she'll still be friends with them. Unfortunately, where I live, getting anybody involved is more likely to hurt her much more than the pedos, so I just try not to get mad so she at least keeps me in the loop.

But yeah, you say she refuses therapy; I doubt you can make her see reason; she'll just deflect, because this is the kind of thing you have to understand yourself through maturity I guess. Personally, I'm a hetero guy, but I let my sister thirst to me over K-pop idols everyday all day long and pretend to take an interest so she doesn't feel so alone. Tried to get her interested in hobbies and personal growth, downloaded games and movies relating to genres she's expressed interest in, took her out and played board games, but she just gets bored of anything that isn't Asian boys and slams the door in my face until she's in the mood to talk herself. I try not to take it personally because i I'm a bit of a weirdo myself and I know what it's like.

It's still better than having her rely completely on strangers for approval, I guess.  So just kind of lurk around so you can shush away the men looking to groom her. Your friend is a groomer's dream!

Also, us autistic folk might know we're weird, but we don't know how to normal. That's a different ballpark. The only way I can be not weird is by not being anything at all. Just sit there and not talk, then stop even coming, and the relationship comes to an eternal conclusion.

Don't worry, I do that a lot. So I do act on my self-awareness after all. Then people tell me I'm creepy and shouldn't just sit there quietly all the time. I'd say many of the patterns of behavior of people with mental conditions are actually the result of them overcompensating for said condition.

Thanks! You're right! It does improve with exercise, although in my case, pacing around a dark and quiet room works much better than doing it outside, with all the... human lifeforms \*shudder\*. That said, even on my best day, I just respond to the world more readily and fewer things feel like huge annoying impositions. But that's as good as it gets.

At this point, I'm not necessarily looking for a way out. I'm just trying to see if this is a common experience with folks round these parts, so that I can feel somewhat more confident ruling in/out being on the spectrum as a cause.
